fine_trace.note: The Ruby input contains a begin/rescue expression in a method with enough local variables to make cursp() exceed 0xff when compiling the rescue handler.
The exception register is taken from the current stack pointer after the many local variables introduced by the input.

fine_trace.code: tmp = genjmp2(s, OP_JMPIF, cursp(), pos2, val);
fine_trace.note: The rescue match emits a conditional jump using cursp() as operand a and the unresolved link head pos2 as the target.
The large register operand selects the extended jump encoding, which must still encode an unresolved jump link with a zero sentinel when pc is JMPLINK_START.
For the extended form this writes the low 16 bits of JMPLINK_START, producing 0xffff instead of the zero link terminator used by gen_jmpdst().
The rescue code patches the linked list of conditional jumps beginning at pos2.
The first dispatch returns pos1+newpos; because newpos is read as -1 from 0xffff, the next position points back into the extended jump operand bytes.
dispatch reads two bytes at the bogus link position; the pointer can address the final byte of the heap instruction buffer, causing a one-byte out-of-bounds read.
